title: Three-factor factor-size-16 beam frontier for product-key state retrieval
question: Can increasing product-key factor granularity from 8 to 16 improve the capability/computation frontier of three-factor addressing at beams 4, 5, and 6?
hypothesis: Finer factor cells should reduce state occupancy enough that a three-factor factor-size-16 configuration can meet the 0.90 capability floor at a lower reranking fraction than the current approximately 0.1543 two-factor robust frontier, while beam expansion controls coverage.

arms.name: three_factor_16_beam4
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 16 and beam 4

arms.name: three_factor_16_beam5
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 16 and beam 5

arms.name: three_factor_16_beam6
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 16 and beam 6

endpoints.name: target_recall_retention_ratio
endpoints.definition: selective target recall divided by exhaustive target recall

decision_rule.condition: Report every registered arm separately at every M with exact pooled target counts, target-recall retention ratio, proposal retention, states scored/M, end-to-end success, arithmetic, pair generation, and occupancy.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific three-factor factor-size-16 capability/computation frontier
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal optimal beam size, semantic retrieval guarantees, asymptotic sublinear scaling, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: An arm satisfies the capability constraint when target-recall retention ratio is at least 0.90 at every registered M level.
decision_rule.licenses: that the arm meets the pre-registered capability floor on the tested workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the arm is generally optimal

decision_rule.condition: An eligible fixed arm improves the current robust two-factor frontier when its mean states_scored_over_M across M={128,256,512} is strictly below 0.1542864583.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that factor-size-16 three-factor addressing improves the currently validated sparse capability frontier on the registered workload and seed set
decision_rule.does_not_license: a general architectural superiority claim or asymptotic scaling

held_constant: factor beam is evaluated only at the registered values 4, 5, and 6
